lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Networks and Staying Safe
lesson.summary: How the internet works, packets, strong passwords, tricky messages and your digital footprint.
learning_objectives: Explain how a message travels across the internet
Make and keep a strong password
Spot tricky messages and think about my digital footprint

standards.text: Understand computer networks including the internet; use technology safely, respectfully and responsibly
Model how information is broken down into smaller pieces, transmitted as packets and reassembled
Discuss real-world cybersecurity problems and how personal information can be protected

success_criteria: I can say what a server, router and packet are
I can explain what makes a strong password
I know what to do about a tricky message
lesson.real_life: Video calls with relatives, school logins and games all use the internet, passwords and safe habits.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how does the internet work, and how do we stay safe?
blocks.say: Today we follow a message across the internet. How do we stay safe on it?

blocks.alt: Rows of blue network cables plugged into a network switch with glowing lights
blocks.caption: Cables link a network switch to many computers.
blocks.credit: Photo by Scott Rodgerson on Unsplash
blocks.say: These cables plug into a network switch. Switches connect the computers in a school network.

blocks.markdown:
A **network** connects computers so they can share. The **internet** joins millions of networks.

A **server** stores a website. A **router** points messages the right way.
blocks.say: A network is a group of computers connected so they can share information. The internet is the biggest network in the world. It joins millions of networks together. When you open a website, your device asks a server. A server is a powerful computer that stores websites and sends them to you. The messages travel along cables, through wireless signals, and through routers that point them the right way.

blocks.markdown:
Messages are split into **packets**. Each packet has an address and a number.

At the end they are put back in order.
blocks.say: Big messages do not travel in one piece. They are split into tiny packets. Each packet has a label saying where it is going and which number it is. Packets can take different routes. At the end, the computer puts them back in order, like a jigsaw. If one packet is lost, only that one needs to be sent again.

scenes.caption: The message.
scenes.say: Here is a message: HELLO FRIEND.

scenes.caption: Three numbered packets.
scenes.say: It is split into three packets. Each one has a number.

scenes.caption: They are put back in order.
scenes.say: They travel by different routes, then are put back in order at the other end. The message arrives safely.

question.prompt: Why is a message split into packets?
question.explanation: Packets are small and are put back in order.

options.text: To make it slower on purpose

blocks.title: Fatima follows a message
blocks.transcript: Fatima sends a message to her cousin in Lahore. It is split into packets. Each packet has an address and a number. They travel by different routes. A switch and a router send each packet the right way. At the other end the packets are put back in order. The message arrives. She uses a long mixed password and keeps it secret. A message says: win a phone, click now! That is a phishing clue. Fatima does not click. She tells her teacher straight away. She thinks before posting. Everything online leaves a footprint.
blocks.caption: Fatima follows a message across the internet and spots a trick.

blocks.markdown:
A **strong password** is long and mixed, and is not easy to guess.

Never share a **password** except with your parent.
blocks.say: A password is a secret key that protects your accounts. A weak password is easy to guess, like 1234 or your name. A strong password is long, has a mix of letters, numbers and symbols, and is not about you. A great trick is to join three random words, like blue elephant pizza. Then add a number and a symbol. It is easy for you to remember but very hard for others to guess.

scenes.caption: Weak: 1234
scenes.say: Here is a weak password. It is short and easy to guess.

scenes.caption: Strong: BlueElephantPizza7!
scenes.say: Here is a stronger one. It joins random words and adds a number and a symbol.

scenes.caption: Strong passwords take much longer to guess.
scenes.say: The longer and more mixed the password, the more guesses a computer would need. The strong one would take far longer to crack.

question.explanation: It is long, mixed and not about you.

instructions: Choose three random words that are not about you.
Add a number and a symbol.
Do NOT use this exact password for real. Only practise the recipe, and keep real passwords secret.

blocks.markdown: Use a different password for each account. Keep it **secret**.
blocks.say: A strong password is only useful if it stays secret. Do not write it where others can see. Do not use the same password everywhere, because if one is stolen, all your accounts are at risk. Ask a parent to help you use a password manager. And never tell your password to a friend or a stranger.

blocks.markdown:
**Phishing** messages try to trick you into sharing private details.

Do not click, do not reply. Tell a grown-up.
blocks.say: Some messages online are tricks. A scam message might say you won a prize. It may ask you to click a link and type your password. This is called phishing, like fishing for your details. Clues are strange spelling and a rush to act now. Another clue is an offer too good to be true. The safe move is to not click, not reply, and tell a grown-up.

blocks.caption: A tricky message is like bait on a hook.

blocks.markdown:
Your **digital footprint** is the trail you leave online.

Think before you **post**: it can stay for a long time.
blocks.say: Every time you go online you leave a trail, like footprints in the sand. Photos you post, comments you write and sites you visit can stay for a long time. This trail is called your digital footprint. Some of it is positive, like a nice message. Some can be harmful if it shares private things. Before you post, pause and think: would I be happy for my family and teacher to see this?

blocks.alt: Everything we post leaves a footprint.
blocks.caption: Everything we post leaves a footprint.

question.explanation: It is the trail we leave online.

options.text: The trail of things you leave online

blocks.text: Stop 2: Being kind and responsible online

blocks.markdown: Be **kind** online. Tell a grown-up if something upsets you.
blocks.say: Be as kind online as you are in person. Do not post unkind comments. Do not share other people's photos without asking. If someone is unkind, or you see something upsetting, tell a grown-up. Save the evidence and do not reply with anger. Every one of us can make the internet a kinder place.

blocks.alt: Be kind and ask before sharing.
blocks.caption: Be kind and ask before sharing.
blocks.say: Kind words and asking before sharing make the internet a nicer place.
